method: One generation of a runner seen from straight in front, coming toward the viewer, with the canonical athlete and the released easy run pose attached. Near-black pixels were clamped to pure black. stride-mirrored.png is that image flipped left to right: from the front, the mirror is the other step. Frames 1, 3 and 5 are stride.png; frames 2, 4 and 6 stride-mirrored.png. Nothing was redrawn by hand.
prompt: Educational running form illustration, one single pose. Reference the first attached image for the athlete's exact identity: faceless bald white/light-grey anatomical athlete, fine dark contours, smooth neutral featureless pelvis, white trainers. Match the second attached image's rendering style and muscle colours exactly (it is the same athlete running, seen from the side). Camera: DIRECTLY IN FRONT of the runner at chest height, perfectly centred, the runner coming straight toward the viewer, so the drawing is left-right balanced. Pose, mid-stride: the leg on the viewer's LEFT is driven forward with its knee raised to about hip-flexion 60 degrees and its foot tucked under, while the leg on the viewer's RIGHT is planted with its foot landing directly under the hips, knee softly bent. Arms bent about 90 degrees and swinging front to back, never across the body: the arm on the viewer's RIGHT is forward toward the viewer, the arm on the viewer's LEFT is back. Tall torso, shoulders relaxed and level, head level, hands loose. Muscle colours: strongest purple on the glutes, quadriceps, hamstrings and calves; pale lilac on the hip flexors and core; every other muscle white-grey. Square canvas, the whole figure about 80% of the height, centred, both feet inside the frame. Pure solid black background. One person only, no extra limbs. No floor line, road, shadow, scenery, motion lines, labels, text, logos or arrows.
